lead: New Orleans plumbing deals with heat, heavy rain, hurricanes, sinking ground and very old houses. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across New Orleans.
risk: broken lines from settling soil, old cast-iron and galvanized pipe, and storm flooding
risk_short: settling soil, old pipes and flooding
why: New Orleans has some of the oldest homes in the country. Shotguns and Creole cottages often sit on piers, with exposed galvanized lines and cast-iron drains. Soft soil settles over time and breaks water and sewer lines.
Heavy rain and hurricanes flood streets and push water back into homes. Raised homes have exposed pipes that can freeze in rare hard cold.
utility: Sewerage and Water Board of New Orleans (SWBNO)
water: The Sewerage and Water Board treats Mississippi River water. It is moderately hard. Boil water advisories happen after pressure drops, so watch for notices.
tips: Sign up for city alerts about boil water advisories.
Wrap exposed pipes under raised homes before a freeze.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Scope the sewer line before buying.
areas: PipeMend works in the French Quarter, the Garden District, Uptown, Mid-City, the Marigny, Bywater, Gentilly, Lakeview and every other New Orleans neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the New Orleans Department of Safety and Permits, and plumbers must be licensed by the State Plumbing Board of Louisiana.

faq.q: Why do New Orleans pipes break so often?
faq.a: Much of the city sits on soft soil that slowly sinks. Settling stresses water and sewer lines until joints pull apart. Older homes with rigid pipes feel it most.
